review: For three boundary extras with U and V at the boundaries, the two-vertex end requires at least five grid vertices and the three-vertex end at least four. Grid paths cannot span both ends.

With one interior extra X, layers two/three give degree at most three. At layer one, degree four forces both left boundary neighbours and two grid neighbours; X cannot meet row one. Row-one and column-one paths require five vertices each and cannot coincide by endpoint/middle support. Reversal covers layer four.

If the private vertex at the enlarged boundary is interior, its layer-two degree is deficient. At layer one, row-one paths need at least four grid vertices and column-one paths at least five. Their endpoint/middle support again proves disjointness.
These alternatives exhaust all distributions of the three extra vertices, including an interior private vertex. All arguments concern additional edges after removing the saturated parent incidences.
accepted_scope: Exactly 21 vertices in six nonsingleton BFS layers imply m<=7 in the adjacent-ball grid.
